canonical_statement: The study evaluated cyclosporine as an alternative treatment for drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS) syndrome and compared clinical course with systemic corticosteroid-treated controls.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: While cyclosporine represents an alternative treatment for DRESS, little is known about its utility.

canonical_statement: This was a retrospective case-control study at Massachusetts General Hospital and Brigham and Women’s Hospital using records from January 1, 2008, through May 1, 2019.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This was a retrospective case-control study of adult patients admitted to Massachusetts General Hospital or Brigham and Women’s Hospital from January 1, 2008, to May 1, 2019.

canonical_statement: Eligible patients were adults with DRESS diagnosed by dermatology consultation and a RegiSCAR score greater than 5, corresponding to definite DRESS in the study definition.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Patients with a European Registry of Severe Cutaneous Adverse Reactions (RegiSCAR) score greater than 5 were included.

canonical_statement: The analyzed cohort included 26 patients: 5 treated with cyclosporine and 21 treated with systemic glucocorticoids.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The data from 5 patients treated with cyclosporine and 21 patients who received systemic glucocorticoids were analyzed.
